negative_reviews.author: Blossom2k4
negative_reviews.text: I haven been around 5 times, one time my friend fell ill with food poisoning thought nothing of it because ive been so many times. Last night i went and i have never felt so sick in my life. Truly disappointed especially after being so many times.

negative_reviews.author: Ashley Morris
negative_reviews.text: Food is ok but they put you on tables that are so close together it’s like eating on Ryanair. Then they slap on a service charge like its American despite staff being on a living wage in the UK!

negative_reviews.author: Nikki
negative_reviews.text:
ラーメンは、種類は豊富にあるけど麺がスープと絡まなく、感動はない。スープ自体はユニークで美味しいのに、麺が味を引っ張ってもったいないと感じた。
Hell Ramenは豚骨スープに辛味を足したような味で美味しかった。それゆえに、麺さえもっと質が高ければ、値段相応あるいはそれ以上の感動を得られるのに...と残念に思った。

客の入店時に太鼓を毎度叩いているようで、店内が広いからか音が響いて、個人的には騒音だった。音が鳴るたびに驚いて入口を見る他のお客さんもいたし、日本の飲食店で太鼓を叩く文化はない（お祭りや、あっても居酒屋とか？）ので不思議な印象を受けた。

(Translated by Google)
While there's a wide variety of ramen, the noodles don't blend well with the soup, resulting in a lack of excitement. The soup itself is unique and delicious, but the noodles overpower the flavor, which is a shame.

The Hell Ramen, with its spicy pork bone broth, was tasty. Therefore, I felt it was a pity that if the noodles were of higher quality, it would be worth the price, or even more.

They seem to beat a drum every time a customer enters, and because the restaurant is large, the sound echoes, which I personally found noisy. Other customers were startled and looked towards the entrance each time the drum sounded. Since there's no culture of beating drums in Japanese restaurants (it's more common at festivals or perhaps in izakayas?), it left a strange impression.

negative_reviews.author: Momo
negative_reviews.text:
They say いらっしゃいませ every time new costumers came in. They also play the drum when they do and this big sound makes some customers surprised… mean it made other customers stop eating for a moment. I feel it’s not good for customers to focus on their time and eating.

For foods, their ramen keep the almost same quality with their another branches. ( I had experienced in Edinburgh and Leeds as well)
Even their ramen is not authentic as now Maki and Ramen became kinda “Asian fusion restaurant” (now they have Laksa ramen, Green curry ramen, etc), I recommend here to anyone who got bored of ordinary ramen.
However, if you had already experienced ramens in Japan, it’s better not to expect wonderful moment for their ramen as it’s totally different from real Japanese ramens because of their noodles.

negative_reviews.author: Tanish Tallam
negative_reviews.text: Tried this place based on highly rated reviews, but it did not meet my expectations. It was overpriced, and the staff were not friendly and seemed to be ignoring us. The taste was also not that great.
